title: Fundamentals of Counseling Theories (Advanced Integration)
tagline: From knowing the theories to owning a coherent approach.
welcome: This advanced study takes the theoretical map from CAC.701 and turns it into a working, integrated, defensible clinical identity.
vignette: A supervisee is asked which theory she used in a session. She answers, 'Whichever one the child needed.' Her supervisor smiles and pushes: then show me how you chose. Integration, this course insists, must be reasoned, not improvised.
vignette_attr: A supervision exchange, drawn from practice
description: An advanced, integrative revisit of counseling theories: common factors, principles of eclecticism and integration, comparative case formulation across systems, and the construction of a coherent personal model of practice, with attention to faith-sensitive and culturally responsive integration.
questions: How do I choose between theories in the moment?
What makes integration principled rather than random?
What is my own coherent model?
importance: Unexamined eclecticism risks inconsistent, unfalsifiable practice
Integrated practitioners show better case coherence and confidence
A written personal model is a professional anchor
misconceptions: that integration means using everything, when it means choosing with reasons
that a personal model is fixed, when it is a living document
figures: whose common-factors and integration research grounds the field
whose systematic treatment selection links theory to evidence
outcomes: Evaluate common factors and integration research
You will use the evidence on what makes therapy work.
You will write one case from three theoretical positions.
You will match method to client with explicit reasons.
You will draft and defend your integrative framework.
You will hold conviction and evidence in one model.
You will give and receive rigorous peer critique.
modules: Common Factors and the Case for Integration
Start from what actually makes therapy work.
Name your stance so you can defend it.
Selection with rules is selection you can justify.
Integration must include the whole person and whole client.
The written model is the deliverable of the course.
Critique is the forge of coherence.
assessment: Assessment centers on the personal model.
A written personal theory of practice
tips: Write your model early and revise weekly
Invite critique; it is the fastest teacher
Keep one anchor theory and integrate deliberately
integration: This course completes the theoretical foundation and anchors every clinical course that follows.
faith: We integrate with humility, holding our convictions open to evidence and to God.
closing: May your model be coherent, humble, and alive, and may it serve every child who meets you.
